source: FAO Regional Office for Asia and the Pacific, Swine Health Management, Volume 2: Guide to Prevent and Control Porcine Reproductive and Respiratory Syndrome (RAP Publication 2012/27, Bangkok, 2012)
text: Never feed pigs raw pig meat — the PRRS virus can survive in raw or undercooked meat and infect any pig that eats it. If feeding swill (food scraps) that may contain pig meat or products, it must be cooked thoroughly at a minimum of 100°C for at least one hour before it is given to pigs. This single step significantly reduces the risk of introducing PRRS and several other serious pig diseases through feed.
